answer: A thread holds only while each strand is separately owned, so credit must trace to distinct hands. An identity needs two holders outside its own cluster to countersign its strand, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n separate witnesses rather than one cooperative crew. Each strand is priced by rank: the k-th claim an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A comet audit replays a random strand each epoch, and standing toward the zenith tier survives only while every strand replays.
